back: INTEGER (whole number), REAL (fractional part), CHAR (one character), STRING (text), BOOLEAN (TRUE/FALSE), DATE.
Use a number type if arithmetic is done on the value; use STRING for identifiers such as telephone numbers.
A structure that holds a fixed number of fields, which may have different data types, under one identifier.
One named item within a record.
TYPE TName, then DECLARE Field : Type for each field, then ENDTYPE.
Record.Field ← value; for an array of records use Array[Index].Field.
Array: items of one type, accessed by index. Record: fields of different types, accessed by name.
Related data stays together, the code is easier to read and a record can be passed or stored as one item.
A CHAR is written in single quotes ('B'); a STRING in double quotes ("Harare").
